item.title: Comment on Sanders’ recent victories recall history of prairie socialism by John Lombardo
item.description: Point of order. Bernie Sanders is not a Socialist. Yes, he's progressive and refers to himself as a "democratic socialist," but his politics are a far cry from revolutionary Socialism. We should be educating people on this, because in the unlikely event that he should be elected President, an awful lot of people are going to be disappointed.

item.title: Comment on Socialism is a process, a recognition of possibility by Nat Turner
item.description: A Process or an Event? Bill Fletcher’s definition of socialism as a process should explicitly include socialism as an event. The event is the permanent and lasting demise of Capitalism as a viable economic system, and its replacement by a socialist economy and society. It also includes a radical change in mass psychology, a belief that capitalism is no longer viable. The two cannot really be separated. Like death itself, do we define it as a process or an event? It is both. The debate over what

item.title: Comment on Sanders wins Michigan, Clinton wins Mississippi, Clinton calls for unity by Gabriel Falsetta
item.description: Let's be bold! Let's fight for the first open socialist to run for office since 1983...
